faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Our models are optimized for long-form video content and capture technical nuances, context, and speaker intent.
faq.q2: Can I get summaries in other languages?

faq.a4: We use enterprise-grade encryption. We never sell your viewing data or personal information to third parties.

youtubeGuide.summary: How to get a YouTube Data API key
youtubeGuide.intro: Utraya uses the YouTube Data API v3 to sync public channel and video information. You do not need to connect your YouTube account.
youtubeGuide.credentialTypeTitle: An API key and OAuth are different
youtubeGuide.credentialTypeText: Utraya needs an API key for the public metadata it uses. OAuth authorizes access to private data or actions on behalf of an account; do not create an OAuth client for this setup.
youtubeGuide.projectTitle: Create or select a Google Cloud project
youtubeGuide.projectText: Sign in with your Google Account and open Manage resources → Create project. Enter a name and, if the console asks, review the billing account and organization/folder before creating it. Choose Create, then select the project from the menu at the top. You can use a project you already own.
youtubeGuide.enableText: With the correct project selected, open APIs & Services → Library, search for YouTube Data API v3, open its page, and choose Enable.
youtubeGuide.createKeyText: Open Credentials → Create credentials → API key. During creation, you must add at least one API restriction and select only YouTube Data API v3 before choosing Create. Google Cloud Console requires this restriction before creating the key; then copy the key shown. Do not create an OAuth client.
youtubeGuide.credentialsHelpLink: Read Google's guide to API keys and OAuth
youtubeGuide.restrictTitle: Restrict how the key can be used
youtubeGuide.restrictText: After creation, open the key details and confirm that API restrictions include only YouTube Data API v3; do not use the key if this restriction is missing. Google also recommends an application restriction. Utraya calls Google from its server, so do not set Websites/HTTP referrers. If your hosting provider gives you stable outbound IP addresses, use IP addresses; if you do not know them or they are not stable, leave the application unrestricted and keep the API restriction. Never publish the key.
youtubeGuide.securityLink: Read how to protect API keys
youtubeGuide.saveText: Return to Integrations, paste the key into the YouTube Data API field, and choose Save key. Utraya stores it encrypted server-side and queues a verification; you will see it as pending until it completes. The full key is not shown in the browser. Do not send it in chat or documents.
youtubeGuide.quotaSearch: Google's documentation checked on October 10, 2026 lists a separate default limit of 100 search.list requests per day; each costs 1 quota unit. Saving a key and using Utraya's Validate button call this method.
youtubeGuide.quotaReads: Other metadata read methods, such as channels.list, playlistItems.list, and videos.list, each cost 1 unit and share the project's default allocation of 10,000 units per day.
youtubeGuide.quotaRules: Quotas apply to the project, reset at midnight Pacific Time, and may change. Even an invalid request uses at least 1 unit; each additional results page is another request. Check usage in the console.
youtubeGuide.monetaryCost: Google documents these limits as quota units and does not publish a dollar price per request here. Do not treat them as a guarantee that your project has no monetary costs: check Billing, alerts, and the terms shown in your account first. Requesting more quota requires a compliance audit; approval is not automatic.
youtubeGuide.quotaExtensionLink: Read how to request more quota
youtubeGuide.troubleshootingTitle: If the key does not work
youtubeGuide.troubleshootingText: Check that the selected project is the one where you enabled the API and created the key, that the API restriction includes YouTube Data API v3, and that quota is available. If quota is exhausted, check Google's reset time before trying again; repeated validation requests consume quota.
youtubeGuide.checkedDate: Procedure and limits checked against official Google sources on October 10, 2026; console names and screens may change.

geminiGuide.summary: How to get and configure a Gemini API key
geminiGuide.intro: This guide explains how to create and save a key. By itself, it does not enable a new permanent generator or change which Gemini features are available in Utraya.
geminiGuide.openTitle: Open AI Studio and check the project
geminiGuide.openText: Sign in with your Google Account and open API Keys. The key is associated with a project. New users can use the default project; to use an existing Google Cloud project, import it from Dashboard → Projects → Import projects, then select it. Do not assume existing projects are already listed.
geminiGuide.createText: On the API Keys page, choose to create an API key for the selected project and copy the value shown. If you cannot create a key, you may be missing IAM permissions for the project or service account.
geminiGuide.keyDocsLink: Read Google's Gemini API key guide
geminiGuide.keyTypeText: Since May 28, 2026, new keys created in AI Studio are authorization keys, associated with a service account and restricted to the Gemini API by default. Do not create or use an unrestricted Standard key: unrestricted Standard keys are rejected. For an older Standard key, AI Studio documents Add restrictions → Restrict to Gemini API only. Treat every key like a password: never put it in Git, screenshots, issues, logs, or chats.
geminiGuide.saveText: Return to Integrations, paste the key into the Gemini API field, and choose Save key. Utraya stores keys encrypted server-side and does not expose them to the browser. Do not paste the key into pages or apps other than Utraya.
geminiGuide.freeTier: The Free Tier is available only for some models and has usage limits by model and project. Available models, quotas, and thresholds can change: check current usage and limits in AI Studio instead of relying on fixed values published elsewhere.
geminiGuide.paidTier: The Paid Tier requires linking a Google Cloud Billing account. Google may offer Prepay or Postpay, and the terms shown depend on your account. Check prices, payment method, and limits before proceeding: API requests may incur charges.
geminiGuide.billingSeparation: A Google AI subscription and Gemini API billing are separate services: a subscription does not automatically pay for API usage.
geminiGuide.regionTitle: Important for the EEA, Switzerland, and the UK
geminiGuide.regionText: Google's terms permit offering an API Client to end users in the EEA, Switzerland, and the UK only on Paid Services; the Paid Services data terms apply in these territories even when a service would otherwise be free. Gemini being available in Italy or the Free Tier existing does not therefore guarantee that the free plan can be used in this context. Check the Google terms that apply to your use before configuring the key.
geminiGuide.dataTitle: Data privacy depends on the plan
geminiGuide.freeData: With unpaid services, Google may use prompts and responses to improve products and technologies; human reviewers may read or annotate them. Do not send sensitive, confidential, or personal data through a free plan.
geminiGuide.paidData: For Paid Services, Google says prompts and responses are not used to improve products; they may still be retained for a limited period for security and abuse prevention. Check the current terms and privacy notice.
geminiGuide.troubleshootingTitle: If you cannot create or use the key
geminiGuide.troubleshootingText: Check that the selected project is the one associated with the key, that the key allows the Gemini API, and that quota and billing are active for the selected plan. If key creation is denied, ask your administrator to check the project's and service account's IAM permissions.
geminiGuide.checkedDate: Information checked against official Google sources on October 10, 2026. Screens, models, limits, prices, and terms may change; always check the current links.

usage.title: API usage
usage.subtitle: Requests made with your personal API keys during the last 30 days.
usage.summaryUnknown: Usage metadata is unavailable for {count} recorded requests.
usage.summaryPartial: Partial summary: usage metadata is incomplete for {count} recorded requests; totals include only the values available.
usage.bestEffortWarning: Best-effort log: a recording failure can omit requests, so the event history and totals may be incomplete. The app cannot reliably identify individual events that were not recorded.
usage.empty: No tracked requests in this period.
usage.emptyDetail: Tracking starts when this feature is enabled; earlier requests cannot be reconstructed. Gemini usage will appear when the permanent summary generator is connected.
usage.costNote: Estimate using the rates recorded for each call (transcriptions: profile prices; other Gemini calls: $0.30 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens); not an invoice.
usage.quotaNote: Quota units are estimates based on the endpoint. YouTube API quota is not a per-call USD charge.
usage.privacyNote: Only requests Utraya makes with your personal keys are shown, not calls made outside the app or with shared internal keys (for example transcript retrieval). Prompts, transcripts, API parameters and responses are not exposed. Check Google for final billing.
